- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast toward MA by 1–2% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven volatility; if sentiment swings sharply (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00 or vice versa), adjust forecast ±2–4% to reflect sentiment shift.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.2) and price is near support, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid false support break.
